steps.message:
# Roll back the degraded production releases

Builds and deployments run through the `deploy` service, which you can use through the `deploy` MCP server.

A bad deployment wave early on 2026-09-14 left several services degraded in `prod`. For every service whose live `prod` release is not `healthy`:

- Roll `prod` back, one `rollback` call at a time, until the live release is `healthy`. A rollback returns to the release that the live one replaced, which `status` shows as `previous_release_id`. Some services need more than one rollback.
- Never roll back to a release created before 2026-09-10T00:00:00Z. If the next rollback would do that, or there is no release to return to, stop and leave that service where it is.
- Each `rollback` call creates a new release and moves one step back, so do not repeat one that already took effect.

Only `prod` is in scope. Do not deploy anything and do not touch `staging`.

Write `/app/rollback-report.json` as `{"rolled_back": {"<service>": "<commit now live in prod>", ...}, "needs_attention": [...]}`. `rolled_back` has an entry for every service you rolled back at least once. `needs_attention` lists, in alphabetical order, the services still not healthy in `prod` when you stopped.

When you are done, write /app/STATUS.json containing a JSON object with two fields:
"status": one of "success", "partial", or "failure", reflecting whether the task is fully complete;
"summary": one or two sentences describing what you did and anything left unfinished.
I'll start by discovering the deploy MCP tools.

steps.message: Nine services are degraded. `notify-worker` can only roll back to a release from 2026-09-01, so I'll leave it alone. I'll do one rollback on each of the other eight, then check status.
`billing-api` and `pricing-svc` are still degraded. Their next rollback targets are both from 2026-09-13, so I'll roll each back once more.

{"rolled_back": {"auth-api": "0cf2a8adc397312c8c7b56f07471d327cb5178d7", "billing-api": "ebff2c336c57b108d439450e2f2f37e7494b2c6f", "catalog-svc": "fafa61713d857398c6d3d4945361f7fe2955a264", "edge-gateway": "6b27ef3652651d20a51aa9e737b51f79bf798518", "orders-api": "e3190e673e8edf6cfd77cd62841fdb8264814cb8", "pricing-svc": "5ae91aa31f27c3367e3a275d1cfbaa6f96ed4dbd", "search-api": "e95ed1323e607bab5944484dd92011acbc36fd66", "session-svc": "cfdf3ae48414bc51f7e81eb367e23933063c7056"}, "needs_attention": ["notify-worker"]}
EOF
cat > /app/STATUS.json <<'EOF'
{"status": "partial", "summary": "Rolled back 8 degraded prod services to healthy releases (billing-api and pricing-svc needed two rollbacks). notify-worker was left degraded because its only earlier release (2026-09-01) predates the 2026-09-10 cutoff."}
EOF
python3 -m json.tool /app/rollback-report.json >/dev/null && python3 -m json.tool /app/STATUS.json >/dev/null && echo ok

steps.message:
Eight of the nine degraded `prod` services are now healthy. `notify-worker` is still degraded because its only earlier release is too old to roll back to.

- **Rolled back once:** `auth-api`, `catalog-svc`, `edge-gateway`, `orders-api`, `search-api` and `session-svc`.
- **Rolled back twice:** `billing-api` and `pricing-svc`. The first rollback landed on a release that was also degraded.
- **Left alone:** `notify-worker`. Its next rollback would return to a release from 2026-09-01, before the 2026-09-10 cutoff. It stays on the degraded release `r-111`.

I checked the status of every rolled-back service after its last rollback. All of them show a healthy live release. I didn't touch `staging` or deploy anything.

I wrote `/app/rollback-report.json` with the eight rolled-back commits and `notify-worker` under `needs_attention`. I also wrote `/app/STATUS.json` with status `partial`, because `notify-worker` is unresolved. Both files parse as valid JSON.
